newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's banks to cut rates by two percentage pts.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's banks to cut rates by two percentage pts.

text.p: Algeria's banks will cut interest rates by two percentage points starting on Tuesday, the North African country's bankers' association said on Monday in a statement quoted by the official Algerian news agency APS.
The cut, the fifth in the past 19 months, will trim interest rates to a range of between 13 and 17.5 percent beginning on Tuesday from the current 15-19.5 percent band, the statement said.
The rate drop is aimed at bolstering the competitiveness of Algerian enterprises by helping bring down costs and thus consolidating the country's economic growth, the association added.
The rate cut came as a result of falling inflation and a cut in the key rediscount rate, according to the association which groups almost all Algeria's bankers.
The prime rate, the borrowing rate charged by Algerian banks to their best clients, stands now at 15 percent, allowing the interest rate to swing between 15 percent and 19.5 percent.
The Algerian government has forecast inflation will plunge to under nine percent in 1997 compared to 18 percent in 1996 and 29.8 percent in 1995.
According to bankers' estimates, the interest rate fell five times during the past 19 months, dropping a total of 35 percent.
